Let \(G_\pi\) be the linear map sending \(x\) to \(x^\pi\), and put
\[
B_\pi=G_\pi^T A G_\pi .
\]
Then
\[
\rho(q)=\lambda_{\max}\!\left(A^{-1/2}\Big(\sum_\pi q_\pi B_\pi\Big)A^{-1/2}\right).
\]

The coordinate minimizers are
\[
x_1=-\frac{x_2+x_3}{2},\qquad
x_2=-\frac{x_1+x_3}{2},\qquad
x_3=-\frac{x_1+x_2}{3}.
\]
A direct exact calculation gives the six final-energy matrices:
\[
B_{123}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&0\\0&17/48&5/16\\0&5/16&11/16\end{bmatrix},
\quad
B_{132}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&0\\0&19/36&11/36\\0&11/36&13/36\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
B_{213}=\begin{bmatrix}17/48&0&5/16\\0&0&0\\5/16&0&11/16\end{bmatrix},
\quad
B_{231}=\begin{bmatrix}19/36&0&11/36\\0&0&0\\11/36&0&13/36\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
B_{312}=\begin{bmatrix}19/72&2/9&0\\2/9&5/9&0\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix},
\quad
B_{321}=\begin{bmatrix}5/9&2/9&0\\2/9&19/72&0\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}.
\]

Let
\[
u=\frac{476+\sqrt{17542}}{1659},\qquad
w=\frac12-u,
\]
and choose
\[
q_{123}=q_{213}=u,\qquad q_{312}=q_{321}=w,\qquad q_{132}=q_{231}=0.
\]
For this distribution the space splits into the antisymmetric line \((1,-1,0)\) and the symmetric plane \((r,r,z)\). On the antisymmetric line the generalized eigenvalue is
\[
\frac{(1,-1,0)^T M(1,-1,0)}{(1,-1,0)^T A(1,-1,0)}
=\frac{3}{16}-\frac{u}{48}.
\]
On the symmetric plane the top eigenvalue is the same exactly when
\[
1659u^2-952u+126=0,
\]
whose feasible root is the \(u\) above. Therefore
\[
\rho_*=\frac{3}{16}-\frac{u}{48}
=\frac{14455-\sqrt{17542}}{79632}.
\]

For optimality, take
\[
z=-\frac{62}{27}-\frac{2\sqrt{17542}}{189},
\qquad
a=(1,-1,0),\qquad y=(1,1,z),
\]
and
\[
R=\frac{30685}{243}+\frac{2188\sqrt{17542}}{1701},\qquad
X=\frac{Raa^T+yy^T}{R\,a^TAa+y^TAy}.
\]
Then \(X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{tr}(AX)=1\), and exact substitution gives
\[
\operatorname{tr}(B_{123}X)=\operatorname{tr}(B_{213}X)
=\operatorname{tr}(B_{312}X)=\operatorname{tr}(B_{321}X)=\rho_*,
\]
while
\[
\operatorname{tr}(B_{132}X)=\operatorname{tr}(B_{231}X)
=\rho_*+\delta,\qquad \delta>0.
\]
Thus for every distribution \(q\),
\[
\rho(q)\ge \operatorname{tr}\!\left(\sum_\pi q_\pi B_\pi X\right)\ge \rho_*.
\]
So the displayed distribution is optimal.

Equality forces \(q_{132}=q_{231}=0\). Also \(M\preceq \rho_* A\) and \(\operatorname{tr}((\rho_*A-M)X)=0\), so \((\rho_*A-M)a=0\). From the third coordinate this gives \(q_{123}=q_{213}\), and from the first two coordinates it gives \(q_{312}=q_{321}\). Finally the antisymmetric eigenvalue condition gives \(q_{123}=u\). Hence the minimizer is unique.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{14455-\sqrt{17542}}{79632},\frac{476+\sqrt{17542}}{1659}\right)}.
\]
